Subject: Production impact after 13b upgrade — latency and content regressions

Camila —

Quick note from our SREs: after we flipped to the new model/quant bundle (redwood-13b-v2-q4_0) at ~02:00 UTC this morning, we see P95 latency climb from ~120ms to ~320ms and a throughput collapse of ~30% on our standard inference pool. Error rate for generation requests rose from 0.5% to 3.2% and we observed a few customers reporting increased hallucinations in the Safety channel.

I attached compressed traces and a short sample of hallucinated responses. This is causing a visible degradation in our product demo flows and a handful of enterprise customers flagged the issue to our CS team. Can Redwood prioritize? We need a short-term mitigation (rollback or routing) and a timeline for full remediation.

Thanks,
Gretchen Ames

Thanks for the ping — quick initial triage below.

Summary of findings (first 90m):
- Reproduced P95 increase locally when running redwood-13b-v2-q4_0 with Helion's prompt distribution; p95 moved from ~110ms -> ~310ms at target concurrency.
- Kernel-level contention observed on broadcast ops in the attention kernels when sequence length > 512; with q4_0 we see more frequent dequantization/quantization boundaries which increases instruction cache pressure.
- KV cache behavior: we saw higher-than-expected cache re-allocations when Helion's client-side prefix-caching interacts with our batching window; combined with q4 rounding errors some cache entries re-evaluate which increases per-request work.

Recommended immediate mitigations (ordered):
1) Short-term: Route Helion to redwood-13b-v2-fp16-hosted (no quant) for 6-12 hours while we collect extended traces — low risk, increases cost but buys time.
2) Medium-term (24-48h): Roll back quant profile to q3_0 on their dedicated pool and deploy a kernel patch that reduces dequantization frequency for long sequences.
3) Long-term: Add a quantization-stability flag that forces consistent dequant alignment and improve prompt-length-aware batching heuristics.

ETA: I can push the hosted routing change in ~45 minutes if we get thumbs up from sales/ops (need priority capacity). Kernel patch scope looks like 36-72 hours to validate.

Attachments: brief-triage-notes.txt; I pushed an incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-789

-Markus
